actions.reason: For long sequences (256 ids or more, e.g. BasicTokenizer.encode), apply_merges now applies the merges in rank order using str.replace on a code-point string, instead of the Python heap loop. This is exact: merging rank r only creates pairs that contain token r, and all of those have ranks above r. So the lowest rank present never goes down, and applying each merge once in rank order (left to right, non-overlapping, like merge()) gives the same result. The fast path is guarded: every merge (a, b) -> idx must have 0 <= a, b < idx, ranks must be distinct, and every id and rank must fit in a code point. If any check fails it falls back to the existing heap path. Evaluation: outputs identical, encode_ir 0.9824.
